educationTaxCredit.salaryHint: Your salary minus non-taxable allowances such as meal allowance. This sets how much tax you owe.

school.hint: Up to 3M KRW per student a year · private academy fees do not count

univ.label: University student
univ.hint: Up to 9M KRW per student a year · graduate school counts only for yourself

disabled.label: Special education for a disabled person
disabled.hint: No limit · rehabilitation education for a parent counts too

grad.label: University or graduate school tuition
grad.hint: Courses of one semester or more and part-time courses, minus scholarships and employer support

training.label: Vocational training fees
training.hint: Minus any support from employment insurance and the like

loan.label: Student loan repayments
loan.hint: Tuition loan principal and interest repaid this year, excluding late fees and amounts forgiven or repaid with local government support

exam.label: CSAT fee and university application fees
exam.hint: College Scholastic Ability Test fee and university admission screening fees

care.label: Kindergarten or daycare costs
care.hint: Tuition, childcare fees, meals and after-school programs (books included)

academy.label: Private academy and sports facility fees
academy.hint: Monthly courses held at least once a week. Example: 200,000 KRW a month × 12 = 2.4M KRW

school.label: School tuition, meals, textbooks, after-school classes

trip.label: Field trips
trip.hint: School trips and camps that are part of the curriculum, up to 300,000 KRW per student a year

arts.label: Arts academy and sports facility fees
arts.hint: Monthly courses held at least once a week at arts academies (piano, art) or sports facilities (taekwondo, swimming). Academic tutoring such as English or math does not count

uniform.label: School uniforms
uniform.hint: Middle and high school only, up to 500,000 KRW per student a year

tuition.label: University tuition and entrance fees
tuition.hint: Subtract scholarships and anything your child paid with a student loan

special.label: Rehabilitation education for a disabled person

status.none: Enter education costs to see the credit and how much tax it saves.
status.noTax: The credit is {credit} KRW, but your tax due is already 0, so nothing comes back.
status.standard: The standard tax credit of 130,000 KRW beats the {credit} KRW education credit, so the education credit does not reduce your tax.
status.partial: The credit is {credit} KRW, but your tax due is smaller, so only {saving} KRW comes off. Unused credit is not carried forward.
status.full: Your tax falls by the {credit} KRW credit plus 10% local income tax.

who.title: Whose education costs count
items: Your own education costs have no limit: university and graduate school tuition, vocational training fees (minus support) and student loan repayments.

Costs you paid for your spouse, children, siblings, adopted or foster children count. From payments made on or after January 1, 2026 there is no age or income test, so a university student with a part-time job still counts (Income Tax Act Art. 59-4(3), amended December 23, 2025).
Education costs for parents or grandparents do not count, except rehabilitation education for a disabled person.
A dependant's graduate school costs and tuition your child paid with a student loan do not count. Your child claims the loan later, as their own education cost, when repaying it.
Leave out anything paid with tax-free money such as scholarships or employer tuition support.
For dual-income couples, a child's education costs go to the parent who claims that child's basic deduction.

list.title: What counts and what does not

rows.item: School, kindergarten and daycare tuition, entrance fees, meals, textbooks, after-school classes
rows.note: Books for after-school classes included. 3M KRW per child for preschool to high school (Enforcement Decree Art. 118-6(1) 1-3, 5)

rows.item: Private academy and sports facility fees for preschool children
rows.note: Monthly courses held at least weekly (Income Tax Act Art. 59-4(3)1(d), Decree Art. 118-6(7))

rows.item: Arts academy and sports facility fees for grade 1-2 (or under 9)
rows.note: Payments from 2026. Monthly, at least weekly, combined with school costs up to 3M KRW (Art. 59-4(3)1(e), Decree Art. 118-6(8)-(10))
Up to 500,000 KRW per student a year (Decree Art. 118-6(1)4)
Part of the school curriculum, up to 300,000 KRW per student a year (Decree Art. 118-6(1)6)

rows.item: CSAT fee and university application fees

rows.note: Up to 9M KRW per student a year (Art. 59-4(3)1 proviso)

rows.item: Your own graduate school, vocational training and student loan repayments
Rehabilitation education for a disabled person
rows.note: No limit, parents included, minus government support (Art. 59-4(3)3, Decree Art. 118-6(14))

rows.item: Academic tutoring for school students (English, math, etc.)
rows.note: Only preschool academies and grade 1-2 arts and sports classes count

rows.item: Arts classes for grade 3 and above

rows.note: Uniforms count only for middle and high school (Decree Art. 118-6(1)4)
Graduate school counts only for yourself (Art. 59-4(3)1 proviso)

rows.item: Tuition your child paid with a student loan
rows.note: Your child claims it when repaying (Art. 59-4(3)1 proviso, 2(d))
Except rehabilitation education for a disabled person (Art. 59-4(3)1, 3)

rows.item: Amounts paid with tax-free scholarships or employer tuition support

missing.title: Costs missing from the simplified service and receipts
items: Only kindergartens, schools, daycare centers, vocational training institutions and student loan agencies must submit data to the simplified service (Enforcement Decree Art. 216-3(1)4).
Private academies and sports facilities do not have to. For preschool and grade 1-2 classes, get an education fee payment certificate from the academy or gym and give it to your employer.
If uniform purchases are missing, get a receipt with the student's name from the uniform shop.
If field trip costs are missing, ask the school for a payment receipt.
Data for adult children or a spouse only appears after that person consents to sharing it on Hometax.

yearEnd.desc: Carry your education costs over and estimate your full refund

dependent.title: Dependent Deduction Checker
dependent.desc: Whoever claims the child's basic deduction also gets the education credit

card.desc: Academy fees and uniforms paid by card also count as card spending (school fees do not)

medical.title: Medical expense tax credit
medical.desc: 15% of family medical costs above 3% of gross pay
